summary: TonersCart v2 backend testing complete. 46/46 pytest tests passed (36 regression from iteration_3 + 10 new v2 tests covering Refilled toner_type re-enabled, extended supplier signup payload (state/pincode/cities_served/pan_number/years_in_business/seller_types/compatible_brands/testing_before_delivery), POST /api/auth/supplier-documents auth-gated patch, GET /api/admin/suppliers/{id}/documents (signed URLs + ai_check structure), approve copying new fields to suppliers table, reject with rejection_reason, and Refilled-bad → 400). No regressions. Email send (Resend) and AI doc check are best-effort and do not throw on no-op/empty docs.

minor.issue: Endpoint signature requires require_user; any authenticated user can patch ONLY their own user_id row (server uses user['id']) — that's safe. No explicit role check, so a customer or admin could call it but it would only update their own pending row (which they wouldn't have). Acceptable.
Carried from iteration_3 — returns supplier_status='pending' even with no suppliers_pending row. No UX impact since signup always creates the row.
Carried from iteration_3 — non-atomic stock decrement (read-then-write); risk of oversell under concurrency.
Email send to support@tonerscart.com is best-effort (try/except, logged). Resend is configured but in test mode emails may not deliver — verified endpoint returns 200 without exceptions, per spec.

action_items: Optional: tighten supplier-documents auth so only role=supplier can call it (purely defensive — current behavior is functionally safe).
Carry-over from iteration_3: atomic stock decrement on POST /api/orders.
Carry-over from iteration_3: distinguish 'not_applied' vs 'pending' supplier_status.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~709 lines (up from ~560). Strongly consider splitting into routers: auth.py, listings.py, orders.py, admin.py, chat.py — file size threshold (>700) is hit.

supplier-documents PATCH stores raw paths trusted from client (e.g. '<uid>/gst.pdf') without verifying the path prefix matches user['id']. A malicious supplier could write a path pointing to another user's storage prefix. Recommend asserting path.startswith(f"{user['id']}/") for each non-empty doc field.

_run_ai_check is awaited inside signup endpoint (not actually fire-and-forget despite the comment) — adds latency to signup. Wrap in asyncio.create_task or background_tasks.add_task to make it truly non-blocking.
DOC_FIELDS list duplicated between server.py and SupplierDocPaths model — single source of truth would help.
approve copies new fields but does not copy doc_* paths to suppliers table — if business needs to retain references post-approval, consider copying or keeping a join.
CORS still allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True (browsers reject combo).
